- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 10–20% for the next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.67) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 15–30% for the next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in true outcome (e.g., >20% above recent mean), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x the recent 7-day average.  
- If model forecast is below 1.0x recent 7-day average and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model is likely underestimating; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 3 days.  
- If model forecast is above 1.5x recent 7-day average and sentiment is negative, model is overestimating; reduce by 0.2–0.5 for next 5 days.  
- Model tends to lag in correcting for sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day delay in adjusting forecasts when sentiment changes direction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; reduce first 5 forecasts by 10–15%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overreact; apply a 20–30% downward correction to all forecasts.
